title: katam room (katam-room/1)
description: One room: its size, art, collision, objects, doors and properties. Coordinates: cells are 16x16 px, (0,0) top-left, x right, y down; objects are in pixels. A room is at least one screen (15x10 cells) and width*height must not exceed 1950 cells. See docs/design/authoring/rooms.md and docs/design/authoring/AI-GUIDE.md.

id.description: This room's id; must match the file path: rooms/<area>/<name>.room.json has id "room:<area>/<name>".

name.description: Human-readable name (not used by the game).

description.description: Free text: intent, notes for the next editor or model (not used by the game).

bind.description: Numeric ids in the game. Vanilla rooms carry them so they compile to the same slots; new rooms omit bind and the compiler allocates.

content.description: Index shared by the room's tilemap, collision, object, progress and nav tables (vanilla: 0-286).

size.description: Room size in 16-px cells. The fg tilemap is twice this in 8-px tiles. One screen is 15x10 cells.

area.description: New rooms only: the world area the game files the room under (the AI helpers' room graph and the pause screens' area lookup, gUnk_08D6CD0C.unk46). Default: the area of the vanilla room the first door leads to, else rainbow_route. Vanilla rooms ignore it (their area comes from the game).

extraBgOffsetX.description: Constant horizontal scroll offset of the extra layer (HW BG2), added after the parallax term in camera-parallax mode (priorityFlags bit 1 clear). The extra layer is never instantiated in retail data (objectList2Idx is 0xFFFF everywhere). Unit: px. Neutral value 0. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.unk02; omitted = 0.

extraBgOffsetY.description: Constant vertical offset of the extra layer (HW BG2): subtracted from its bottom-anchored scroll Y, so a positive value shows N more pixels of the layer's top (the image moves down on screen). Camera-parallax mode only. Code-only: the extra layer is never instantiated. Unit: px. Neutral value 0. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.unk04; omitted = 0.

extraBgScrollX.description: Extra layer (HW BG2) horizontal scroll parameter, dual-purpose: with priorityFlags bit 1 clear it is the parallax ratio (8.8, 0x100 = moves 1:1 with the camera); with bit 1 set it is added to the layer's scroll every frame (auto-scroll velocity). Copied to LevelInfo.unk_S16Vec2_B4.x at load. Note the C name is misleading: _06 is X, _08 is Y. Unit: fx8.8 ratio (bit1 clear) | fx8.8 px/frame (bit1 set). Neutral value 256. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.unkXmod_06; omitted = 256.

extraBgScrollY.description: Extra layer (HW BG2) vertical counterpart of unkXmod_06: parallax ratio (8.8) in camera mode, per-frame velocity with priorityFlags bit 1 set. Unit: fx8.8 ratio (bit1 clear) | fx8.8 px/frame (bit1 set). Neutral value 256. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.unkXmod_08; omitted = 256.

bgOffsetX.description: Constant horizontal offset of the background layer (HW BG0) in camera-parallax mode: bgScrollX = cameraX*ratio + unk0A. Original-code quirk: the load-time seed copies it WITHOUT the *0x100 (level.c:223), the per-frame formula with it; harmless because the next frame recomputes, and invisible because it is 0 everywhere. Keep the quirk when porting. Unit: px. Neutral value 0. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.unk0A; omitted = 0.

bgOffsetY.description: Vertical offset of the background layer (HW BG0). The background's scroll Y is anchored so that the background's bottom edge meets the screen's bottom edge when the camera is at the bottom of the room; unk0C is subtracted from that, so the background image sits unk0C pixels lower on screen (shows more of its top). Used both at load and every frame (camera-parallax mode). Unit: px. Neutral value 0. (registry confidence: confirmed) Same as raw.unk0C; omitted = 0.

bgScrollX.description: Background layer (HW BG0) horizontal scroll parameter. With priorityFlags bit 2 clear (camera-parallax mode, 285/286 rooms) it is the parallax ratio in 8.8 fixed point: 0x100 = the background moves 1:1 with the camera, 0x40 = a quarter as fast, 0 = fixed. -1 = derive it at load as (bgWidthPx - 240) / 2160, i.e. map 9 screen-widths of camera travel onto the background's full width (0x870 = 9 * 240). If the background is no wider than the screen the ratio is forced to 0. With bit 2 set it is instead added to the background's scroll every frame (auto-scroll velocity, 8.8 px/frame). Unit: fx8.8 ratio (bit2 clear) | fx8.8 px/frame (bit2 set). Neutral value -1. Special values: -1 = derive from background width: (bgWidthPx - 240) * 256 / 0x870. (registry confidence: confirmed) Same as raw.unk0E; omitted = -1.

bgScrollY.description: Background layer (HW BG0) vertical scroll parameter; same scheme as unk0E. Ratio mode: 8.8 ratio applied to the camera's distance from the room's bottom edge; -1 = derive as (bgHeightPx - 160) / 1440 (0x5A0 = 9 * 160); forced to 0 when the background is no taller than the screen. Velocity mode (priorityFlags bit 2): added to the scroll Y every frame. Unit: fx8.8 ratio (bit2 clear) | fx8.8 px/frame (bit2 set). Neutral value -1. Special values: -1 = derive from background height: (bgHeightPx - 160) * 256 / 0x5A0. (registry confidence: confirmed) Same as raw.unk10; omitted = -1.

playfieldBehindExtraLayer.description: BG priority: set -> playfield (BG3) priority 2 and extra layer (BG2) priority 1, so the extra layer draws in front of the playfield and the playfield drops behind priority-1 sprites; clear -> BG3 priority 1, BG2 priority 2. Set in every retail room (the extra layer never exists, so in practice it only sets the playfield's priority relative to sprites). The port renderer also reads it (platform/render/rl_build.c). Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: confirmed) (mask 0x0001)

extraBgAutoScroll.description: Extra layer (BG2): add unkXmod_06/08 to its scroll every frame instead of camera parallax. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (mask 0x0002)

bgAutoScroll.description: Background layer (BG0): unk0E/unk10 are a per-frame scroll velocity instead of parallax ratios. Only room 919 (Dark Mind sky) sets it, with velocity 0/0: the room freezes the parallax so its own code (code_080023A4.c, case 919) can drive the background scroll directly. (registry confidence: confirmed) (mask 0x0004)

phoneCallAllowed.description: The cell phone works here: pressing R with battery calls the CPU helper Kirbys (sub_08056C2C, SE_KIRBY_CALL, consumes a battery), and the HUD shows the phone icon only in rooms with this bit. Clear only in room 919 and the credits rooms 980-982. (registry confidence: confirmed) (mask 0x0008)

answerCallAllowed.description: Responding to another Kirby's phone call works here: while a call is pending (gUnk_02021580 = caller's player id, set when the caller's call completes, kirby.c sub_080572A0), pressing R in a room other than the caller's (or when the caller is dead/out) warps this Kirby to the caller via sub_08056C2C; the HUD shows the incoming-call indicator only when this bit is set. Same rooms as bit 3 in retail data, so data cannot separate them; only the call sites do. (registry confidence: likely) (mask 0x0010)

returnToHubAllowed.description: Holding L returns Kirby to the hub: newly pressed L (unk11A & 0x200) enters sub_08056E40 (phone animation, SE_KIRBY_CALL, no battery cost, unkC |= 0x40000); holding L for 48 frames continues to sub_0805BEE8 -> sub_08057774, which sets roomId = 801 and warps. Clear in the hub/tutorial (801, 803-805), the final area (909-919), minigame/rematch rooms and the credits. (registry confidence: confirmed) (mask 0x0040)

roomFlags.description: Room behaviour bits. Misnamed in C: only bit 0 is about BG priority. Bits 1-2 select auto-scroll for the two background layers, bits 3/4/6 gate the cell-phone (R) and return-to-hub (L) actions. Retail data uses only 0x79 (262 rooms), 0x19 (11), 0x39 (9), 0x01 (3) and 0x25 (1). Exhaustive search of game/src for priorityFlags: masks 1, 2, 4, 8, 0x10, 0x40 only. Neutral value 121. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.priorityFlags.

raw.description: Room properties by their C field name, for fields the registry has not named. Always accepted, even after a field gets a name.

fgLayerRoomTag.description: Advanced: the room-id annotation in the playfield layer header; defaults to this room's numeric id.

art.description: The playfield art (HW BG3), one legend key per 16x16 cell. Each legend value is a metatile: four 8x8 tile tokens from the room's tileset. Art is separate from collision: what you see vs. what is solid.

collision.description: What each 16x16 cell is to physics, one legend key per cell. Conventional keys: "." empty, "#" solid, "=" one-way platform, "~" water, "^" hazard, "%" breakable, "D" door cell, "H" ladder; the legend decides.

patches.description: Cell changes the game applies at run time to a cell (e.g. a breakable block turning into air): new art and new collision for one cell. Several on one cell apply in order.

tiles.description: New art for the cell: TL TR BL BR.

key.description: Advanced: the collision value that selects this patch; derived from the grid (and earlier patches on the cell) when omitted.

doors.description: Door transitions: standing on one of `cells` and entering takes Kirby to `arrive` in room `to`. Order matters: it is the order of the per-room save bits (chests first, then doors), so append rather than reorder in an existing room. Most doors need a door-typed collision value under their cells and often a door object for the graphics.

arrive.description: Where Kirby arrives in the destination room, in 16-px cells: the cell he lands ON (in vanilla, the floor cell right under the destination door), so the cell above it must be empty.

cells.description: The cells of this room that act as the door.

flags.description: Door behaviour bits (Unk_0888562C_3.unk0C): 0x80 = do not move the respawn point; 0x01 / 0x02 = arrive facing one way / the other (docs/naming/doors.md). Omitted = 0.

cellFlags.description: Advanced: per-cell flags when they differ between cells of one door.

objects.description: Things placed in the room: enemies, items, chests, gadgets, triggers. Positions are pixels (cell * 16 + 8 is a cell centre). Order is the spawn order.

movePattern.description: Movement pattern, switched in CreateWaddleDee and again in sub_080A3CF0 (re-entry after landing / parasol loss). Values >4 fall to default = 0 (one retail record has 5). (registry confidence: confirmed) (template field subtype1)

speed.description: Runtime obj->subtype. Walking speed index for patterns 0/1/2 and the hop: subtype 0..3 -> |xspeed| 0x80/0xC0/0x100/0x180 (0.5/0.75/1/1.5 px per frame). For pattern 1 also the turn period. For pattern 3 it is passed to the parasol as its subtype1 and value 2 keeps the Dee standing after landing. Unit: enum index. (registry confidence: confirmed) (template field subtype2)

paletteVariant.description: Sprite palette variant (generic, object.c sub_0803DFAC). Value 1 on two walkers (subtype2 1 and 2). (registry confidence: likely) (template field unkF)

enemyFlags.description: Generic enemy flag word, read in object.c for every type 0x00-0x64 (ObjType0To37/38To52/53To64). bit0: on death (unk80<=0) the object adds 1 to the per-room-group kill counter gUnk_02023508[unk65E] (read back by OBJ_LEVER_WALL via unkF and by OBJ_OBJECT_SPAWNER). bit1: InitObject sets base.unkC |= 0x1000, which makes ProcessObjectCollisionLists resolve this object against the solid-object list (it is pushed by / can stand on solid objects such as blocks and platforms, like Kirby). bit2: on death, skip sub_08086C48 (the restore-room-music task used after mini-boss fights). bit15 (types 0x00-0x32 only): unkC |= 0x10, the 'Droppy' look: the palette of OBJ_DROPPY is used instead of the type's own. Type-specific code may read further bits. (registry confidence: likely) (template field unk22)

flightPattern.description: Flight pattern, switched in CreateBrontoBurt and in sub_080AD7C0 (resume after being stunned). Values >5 fall to default = 0. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

fast.description: Runtime obj->subtype. Non-zero: horizontal flight speed 0x100 instead of 0xC0, follows a different scripted flight table in the post-rise/dash states; ==1 raises the diagonal-bounce speed from 0xB5 to 0xE2. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

swimPattern.description: Swim pattern, switched in sub_080A712C (descriptor init, called from CreateBlipper via gUnk_08351648[type].unk10) and after re-entering water. Values >4 = 0. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

fast.description: Runtime obj->subtype. Only read by the height-tracking state (pattern 0): non-zero doubles the vertical acceleration (0x18 vs 0xC) and raises the max speed (0x120 vs 0xC0). Retail values 2 and 3 sit on patterns 2 and 3, where nothing reads it. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

fireRate.description: Runtime obj->subtype. 0: never shoots (only plays the 35-frame pulse). Non-zero: each cycle fires a burst of 5 OBJ_GLUNK_BULLETs 12 frames apart; the idle wait between bursts is (3 - subtype) animation loops, so 2 shoots more often than 1. Also copied to the bullet's subtype2. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

movePattern.description: Pattern switch in CreateSquishy. Values >2 = 0. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

fast.description: Runtime obj->subtype. Non-zero: swim 0xC0 instead of 0x80 and leap 0x140 instead of 0x100. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

appearMode.description: 0: hovers in place (scripted bob, gUnk_08353510). Non-zero: hidden ambusher: invisible (flags 0x600) until Kirby is within 10 px horizontally, then reappears at a fixed offset from Kirby and flies vertically toward him; when level it hovers normally. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

Unit: bool. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

(registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

starSubtype.description: Runtime subtype; only passed on as subtype2 of the spawned OBJ_JACK_STAR. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

cannonLockSlot.description: Room state slot (GetStateSlot(STATE_SLOT_ROOM, unk14)) set to 1 while Jack exists and cleared when it is destroyed; 0 = none. spawnTable.description: Which constructor table type indexes: 1 = gSpawnFuncTable1 (all retail data), 2 = gSpawnFuncTable2 (never selected by level data). Neutral value 1. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: confirmed) Omitted = 1.

unk2.description: Which 'already collected / defeated' bitmap unk3 indexes. If the bit is set the object is not spawned. 0 = per room visit (cleared on every room load, 32 bits), 1 = per area (cleared on area change, warp star and some Kirby transitions; used by all food/battery/1UP pickups so they stay collected while you remain in the area), 2 = saved with the file (never used by level data). (registry confidence: confirmed) Omitted = 0.

unk3.description: Bit index in the bitmap chosen by unk2; the object's constructor/defeat code sets it (sub_08001678) so it does not respawn. Must be unique per room (scope 0) or per area (scope 1). (unk2 = 0, unk3 = 31) is the 'no flag' sentinel used by dynamically created objects; level data never uses it, and the defeat counter (unk4) skips objects that carry it. Special values: 31 = with unk2 = 0: no flag. (registry confidence: confirmed) Omitted = 0.

unk4.description: Index of a per-room-visit u32 counter (GetStateSlot(STATE_SLOT_ROOM, unk4), 16 per room slot, zeroed at room load). Defeating an enemy increments its register; gates such as sliding doors, lava walls, scroll locks, Jack, big buttons watch theirs. 0 = none by convention. This is the 'beat all the enemies to open the wall' mechanism, entirely data-driven. Some types reinterpret it (see object_params.json). Neutral value 0. (registry confidence: confirmed) Omitted = 0.

unk5.description: Spawn behaviour bits. (registry confidence: confirmed) Omitted = 0.

unkA.description: No reader found; 0xFF in every record. Preserve. Neutral value 255. No game code reads this. (registry confidence: likely) Omitted = 255.

unkB.description: No reader found; 0xFF in every record. Preserve. Neutral value 255. No game code reads this. (registry confidence: likely) Omitted = 255.

unkD.description: No reader found; 0xFF in every record (likely padding after type). Preserve. Neutral value 255. No game code reads this. (registry confidence: likely) Omitted = 255.
